# Independent audit: optimized triple reflection and extraction through six fibers



I read the complete note and its reflection/extraction dependency, then ran

```
work/math-venv/bin/python supporting computation verify_optimized_triple_six_fiber_extraction.py
```

The verifier passes. Its symbolic identities and exact rational overlap calculations support the following independent geometric and arithmetic checks.

## Actual interval geometry and optimized triple

Positive-length integer fibers of a planar convex body form consecutive integer indices. Their widths form a positive concave sequence. Zero-length boundary fibers may remain geometrically present, but contribute zero to the stated \(H_1\) measure and to the reflection sum.

After translating the middle interval to \([0,b]\), compatibility places the endpoint midpoint interval at \([s,s+(a+c)/2]\), with \(0\le s\le b-(a+c)/2\). The plateau of maximal endpoint overlap is exactly \([s+l/2,s+A/2]\), with \(l=\min(a,c)\), \(A=\max(a,c)\). Each endpoint contributes overlap \(l\) there. Both endpoint inequalities proving intersection with the own-fiber self-overlap level interval are correct. They include equal lengths, collapsed plateaus, and all closed endpoints.

Thus the same actual reflection center retains at least \(2l+\min(b,A)\), while the middle midpoint separately retains \(b\). The stated bound follows. The proposed sharp placement \([0,a],[0,b],[0,c]\) is compatible. If \(A\ge b\), its own midpoint lies on the endpoint plateau. If \(A\le b\), the total overlap decreases just beyond the plateau endpoint; after the endpoint overlap vanishes, the only possible additional maximum is the own-fiber midpoint. This verifies the sharp fixed-length formula, including the case where the own midpoint occurs before the endpoint overlap has vanished.

Other fibers contribute nonnegative additional reflection mass, so using a triple as a lower bound inside a longer support is legitimate.

## Four and five fibers

For four fibers, reversal permits \(b\ge c\), and concavity gives \(d\le c\). Both cases \(a\ge c\) and \(a\le c\) use the correct optimized triple expressions. The comparisons with a largest fiber treat the equality case separately and give strict retention above half when every fiber is strictly lighter than half. The actual four-width example \((1,5,3,1)\) is concave; its complete reflection maxima at the four bases are exactly \((1,5,5,1)\), so the half-retention equality claim is correct.

For any concave sequence, the superlevel set at its third-largest value is consecutive and contains at least three indices. This proves \(R_*\ge3t\) even with ties. The strict superlevel set has at most two indices and can be placed inside an adjacent two-index block.

For five fibers, \(M\le5w_2\) is the usual symmetric discrete concavity inequality. If \(w_2>t\), the two largest entries can be taken at indices \(1,2\) after reversal: an endpoint strictly above its neighbor would force all subsequent widths to decrease, which rules out a larger central value. The ordering \(b,c\ge\max(a,d)\) and \(e\le d\) therefore holds, including ties.

The two triple estimates give precisely \(\min(b,c)+2T\). In the \(b\ge c\) case, the inequalities \(b\le2c-d\), \(e\le2d-c\), and \(c\le2d\) justify every step to \(M\le(7/4)R_*\). In the \(c\ge b\) case, \(c+e\le2d\) and \(b\ge T\) give the stronger \(M\le(5/3)R_*\). There is no reversed concavity sign.

The limiting family \((1+\epsilon,3+\epsilon,2+\epsilon,1+\epsilon,\epsilon)\) is positive and concave for every \(\epsilon>0\). The outer pair at the central base adds at most \(2\epsilon\), and every other possible center base is included in the upper calculation. Thus \(R_*\le4+5\epsilon\) and the lower theorem together prove the sharp limiting fraction \(4/7\). No unproved exact optimizer for \(\epsilon>0\) is used.

## Six fibers and extraction interpretation

All three coefficient identities in equation (4) are correct. The five possible adjacent two-index blocks containing \(\{w_i>t\}\) reduce by reversal to the three listed cases. Each selected quadrature uses only widths at most \(t\), so \(M\le6t\) follows without a missing boundary block or a genericity assumption. Combining it with \(R_*\ge3t\) gives the claimed half bound.

I checked `candidate f9fd3b8e5ea799fa`, particularly its treatment of one positive retained fiber. If the symmetric intersection has two positive fibers it is an actual planar convex body. If it has only one, the thin slab inside the original body retains the entire own interval and has nonempty ambient interior, so it realizes at least the same mass with a true integer-base centroid and local half-depth. Conversely, interval half-depth rigidity makes every admissible extraction's positive-length mixed measure symmetric, bounding it by original reflection retention. Attainment follows from the finite set of possible center bases and continuity of interval overlap on their compact fiber intervals.

The original-source OC consequence uses only the retained source's half-depth and mass at least \(M/2\): each containing cap has original mass at least \(M/4\). The note does not extend the finite-support result to arbitrary numbers of fibers or to higher dimensions. All these scope statements are correct.
